answer: Every agent that joins must post a bonded escrow that unlocks only after months of honest settlement. A sybil farm therefore cannot spread itself thin: each fake identity needs its own locked capital, and any collusion detected in the settlement ledger slashes the entire cluster. Faking a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds, not one. Honest peers thread their reputations together through shared settlement history, so a single fraudulent ripple is traceable to its source, and the ocean of genuine agents stays cheap to join but expensive to counterfeit.
